title: Burst absorption profiles and tenant hedging controller
creator: Miguel Santos
description: Introduce a tenant-facing burst absorption and hedging controller for Dedicated fleets to smooth short-term traffic spikes without violating committed throughput guarantees. The feature combines configurable burst profiles, time-weighted smoothing windows, and speculative slot borrowing with automatic reconciliation to reduce p99 latency regressions during transient surges while protecting long-term contract SLAs.
background: Customers on Dedicated pools commonly see short bursty traffic (e.g., product launches, hourly cron jobs) that temporarily spikes token throughput. Current admission logic is focused on long-term rate guarantees and coarse demotion lanes which either over-shed (impacting customer UX) or allow short-term noisy bursts that cause cross-tenant tail latency violations. We need a middle ground that absorbs bursts predictably and reconciles usage against committed throughput.
problem_statement: How do we allow short bursts above committed throughput in a controlled, observable way so that: (1) critical latency-sensitive requests are not dropped during short spikes; (2) long-run throughput guarantees and billing commitments are preserved; (3) interaction with autoscaler does not cause oscillation or instability?
proposed_solution: Build a Burst Absorption Profile subsystem that: (a) exposes per-tenant burst profile parameters (burst_capacity_seconds, smoothing_window_secs, hedging_priority_weight); (b) maintains a short-lived speculative slot pool on each node for absorbing bursts; (c) enforces a reconciliation ledger that debits speculative consumption and either drains it via throttling or settles against committed buffer tokens over a configurable retroactive window. Combine with a Hedging Controller that temporarily shifts lower-priority work into background lanes during reconciliation rather than shedding outright.
design_notes:
- Per-tenant profile is part of Dedicated tenant config; default conservative profile applied for unmanaged tenants.
- Speculative slots are node-scoped with a global soft cap to avoid cluster-wide exhaustion.
- Reconciliation uses exponentially-weighted moving average (EWMA) of baseline throughput to determine allowable post-burst catch-up rate.
- Integrates with existing routing policy engine via a new admission decision: ALLOW_SPECULATIVE_WITH_LEDGER.
- Metrics emitted: speculative_slots_in_use, speculative_debits_by_tenant, reconciliation_backlog, hedged_requests_count.
- Fallback: if reconciliation backlog exceeds threshold X for Y minutes, escalate tenant to demotion lane and emit incident alert to SRE.
acceptance_criteria: K1: Controlled bursts up to configured burst_capacity_seconds do not increase p99 latency for other tenants by more than 10% in synthetic multi-tenant tests.
K2: Speculative slot usage is correctly debited into the tenant ledger and visible in Console (token / token-second accounting) within 30s.
K3: Reconciliation settles or transitions tenants to demotion within configured window; no unbounded backlog after 2x smoothing_window_secs.
K4: Autoscaler remains stable: no more than 1 scale loop oscillation caused by speculative consumption in 6 hours of load testing.
K5: Feature flags allow per-fleet opt-in and graceful rollback without data loss to ledgers.
rollout_plan: Alpha: enable on internal Dedicated staging fleet behind feature flag; run chaos tests and multi-tenant benchmarks (2 weeks).
Beta: enable for small group of opt-in customers (5-10 fleets) with monitoring dashboards and tailored burst profiles (4 weeks).
GA: open opt-in to all Dedicated customers with recommended profiles and default protection (8 weeks).
Post-GA: evaluate making conservative burst profiles default based on observed safety margin (quarterly review).
testing_plan: Unit tests for ledger accounting, speculative slot allocation and eviction logic.
Integration tests: multi-tenant load generator that emits controlled bursts and validates p99 isolation.
Chaos test: kill nodes while speculative slots are in use to validate ledger durability and reconciliation after restart.
Load test: 48-hour run with synthetic tenants to catch oscillation with autoscaler.
